overview: Black answers 1.Nf3 with 1...b5, grabbing queenside space and aiming the bishop on b7 at the long diagonal and at e4. White can play 2.e4 Bb7 3.Bxb5, taking a pawn, or 2.e3 Bb7 3.Bxb5, as Black gets quick development for the pawn. It is a rare counter-gambit set-up and is dubious in practice.

white_ideas.idea: Take the b5 pawn with Bxb5 or a4 and develop sensibly
Take the centre with e4/d4 and challenge the Bb7

black_ideas.idea: Develop the Bb7 on the long diagonal and play ...e6 and ...Nf6
Hit back at the white centre and play ...a6 and ...c5

typical_structures.structure: Black queenside pawns advanced with a bishop on b7 against a normal White centre

character.notes: Black plays for activity at the cost of a pawn or structure, with unbalanced play.

gambit.notes: The b5 pawn can be taken by Bxb5 and Black plays for development.

soundness.notes: Considered dubious, with White entitled to an edge.

structure.notes: Open diagonals more than a fixed centre.

character.reason: Black gives a pawn for activity.

gambit.reason: The b5 pawn can be captured with Bxb5.

soundness.reason: White is better after the capture.

plans.reason: Black seeks a quick development and a long-diagonal bishop.
